clue.text: Reserve defender no longer on the bench?

parts.note: in football a back is a defensive player, as against a forward
a substitute who is up has left the bench, on their feet and in play

explanation.surface: A football commentator wonders whether the reserve defender has finally been brought on.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that UP is a loose sense: a player no longer sitting on the bench is up and playing.
explanation.definitionFit: A backup is a stand-in kept ready to replace something, just as a reserve is.

clue.text: Apparently hay crop's ruined? Such things are not entirely accepted

definitions.text: Such things are not entirely accepted

parts.note: AP is a short form of apparent or apparently

indicators.note: a ruined crop is wrecked, so these letters are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: A farmer surveys a spoilt harvest and wonders whether the hay is past saving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ruined' gives OCRYPHA. 'Apparently' looks like a surface hedge, but it supplies its abbreviation; the 's is just 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Apocrypha are writings of doubtful authenticity, kept outside the accepted biblical canon.

clue.text: Awkward American trick's ending skating manoeuvre

indicators.note: the ending of a word is its final letter, so only the last of trick's counts

parts.note: a lutz is a figure-skating jump taken off from the back outside edge

explanation.surface: An American skater botches the end of a routine with a clumsy jump.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ending' takes the last letter of trick's, K, before LUTZ.
explanation.definitionFit: Klutz is American slang, from Yiddish, for a clumsy, awkward person.

clue.text: One fruit coming up amidst vegetable garden feature

indicators.note: the reversed pair sits amidst the vegetable, inside its letters

parts.note: a pea is a vegetable

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming up means the words one and fruit are read upwards, backwards

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
a nut is botanically a fruit

explanation.surface: A gardener spots a single fruit sprouting among the vegetable beds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming up' gives TUNI, read upwards in this down clue, and 'amidst' sets it in the vegetable.
explanation.definitionFit: Petunias are popular bedding plants, a feature of many flower beds and borders.

clue.text: Crustacean collapse will come about if biosecurity finally reversed

indicators.note: the collapse comes about, that is around, the reversed letters

parts.note: a crash is a sudden collapse

indicators.note: the words if and the final letter are read backwards
finally picks the last letter of biosecurity

explanation.surface: A warning that a shellfish population will collapse unless biosecurity measures are rolled back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' gives Y and 'reversed' then makes YFI; 'will come about' means the collapse goes around it.
explanation.definitionFit: The crayfish is a freshwater crustacean resembling a small lobster.

clue.text: Party game enciphers wishes in a funny way

indicators.note: something done in a funny way is done oddly, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: At a party, someone encodes their wishes in a comical manner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a funny way' rearranges ENCIPHERS WISHES.
explanation.definitionFit: Chinese whispers is the party game in which a message passed along a line gets garbled.

clue.text: Answer points about origin of extremely discriminatory people

indicators.note: the points go about, around, the single letter

parts.note: gists are main points of an argument

indicators.note: the origin of a word is where it starts, its first letter

explanation.surface: An answer explaining the source of some extremely prejudiced attitudes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'origin of' gives E from extremely, set 'about' by GISTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Ageists are people who discriminate against others on grounds of their age.

clue.text: Excessive coming in to fake name no longer known

indicators.note: the excessive piece comes in, entering the verb for faking

parts.note: to forge is to fake a document or signature
OTT is short for over the top, meaning excessive

explanation.surface: An extravagant forgery of a name that nobody now remembers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming in' makes FORGOTTE before the N; 'to fake' is a verb phrase, so the leaf is the verb, not 'fake' the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Something forgotten has passed out of memory, so is no longer recalled by anyone.

clue.text: No longer a common motivation to train second squad

definitions.text: No longer a common motivation to train

parts.note: a squad is a team

explanation.surface: A coach laments that his second-string squad no longer feels driven to train.
explanation.walkthrough: 'motivation to train' means power to drive a railway train, not urge to practise.
explanation.definitionFit: Steam locomotives once drove most trains but are now a rare sight, kept mostly for heritage lines.

clue.text: Favourite of vegetarians in most of university

indicators.note: the answer sits in the run of letters across these words

explanation.surface: A claim about which food is most popular among students at university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' reveals the letters spanning mosT OF University; 'most of' is not a trimming here.
explanation.definitionFit: Tofu, bean curd, is a staple protein source in many meat-free diets.

clue.text: Cosmetics? Flimsy stuff is vexing

parts.note: toile is a light linen or cotton fabric
tries in the sense of tries one's patience, vexes

explanation.surface: Someone finds the flimsy packaging of beauty products irritating.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits that toiletries stretch beyond make-up.
explanation.definitionFit: Toiletries cover soaps, lotions and other grooming products, a broader family that includes cosmetics.

clue.text: Support a sort of Buddhist quality? That takes effrontery

parts.note: a bra is a supporting undergarment
Zen is a school of Buddhism
the suffix -ness turns an adjective into a noun naming a quality

explanation.surface: Backing a quality of Buddhist calm, someone remarks, would take some nerve.
explanation.walkthrough: ZEN and NESS together read as 'Zen-ness', the quality of being Zen.
explanation.definitionFit: Brazenness is shameless boldness, the same as impudent effrontery.

clue.text: Old bad actors overlooking a measure of resistance

definitions.note: plural answer: ohms are units measuring electrical resistance

indicators.note: to overlook something is to leave it out, so the a is dropped

parts.note: hams are overacting, bad actors

explanation.surface: Veteran poor performers ignore a measure of how much opposition they face.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overlooking' leaves HMS once the A goes.
explanation.definitionFit: The ohm is the SI unit of electrical resistance, so ohms quantify it.

clue.text: Naval officer in a condition to become deserter

indicators.note: the officer goes in, inside, the other letters

parts.note: a state is a condition
PO is a Petty Officer in the navy

explanation.surface: A naval officer in a sorry state ends up deserting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' gives APOSTATE directly; 'to become' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An apostate abandons a religion or cause, deserting what they once held.

clue.text: Trail is enthralling one tense researcher

indicators.note: to enthral is to hold captive, so the trail holds the numeral inside it

parts.note: a scent is the trail an animal leaves
I is the Roman numeral for one
T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: A tense researcher finds a particular trail gripping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'enthralling' gives SCIENT; the 'is' between them in the clue is taken literally.
explanation.definitionFit: A scientist is someone whose work is systematic research into the natural world.

clue.text: Company behind it is involved in odd bits of some TV show

indicators.note: the pair goes into, gets involved in, the other letters
the odd bits are the first and third letters of some
the company comes behind, after, the word it

explanation.surface: A firm stands behind some odd parts of a television programme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odd bits of' some gives S and M; IT then CO go 'involved in' them.
explanation.definitionFit: A sitcom, situation comedy, is a familiar genre of television show.

clue.text: Not unhappy greeting French resort, being in a delicate situation

indicators.note: an unhappy word is out of sorts, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: hi is a greeting
Nice is a resort on the French Riviera

explanation.surface: Someone quite cheerfully hails a Riviera town despite being in an awkward spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not unhappy' looks like a double negative meaning happy; really 'unhappy' rearranges NOT into ONT.
explanation.definitionFit: Skating on thin ice is an idiom for being at risk, so on thin ice means precariously placed.

clue.text: Almost everyone beset by vermin will show hostility

indicators.note: the shortened word is beset, surrounded, by the vermin

parts.note: mice are vermin

indicators.note: almost means one letter short, so the last is cut

parts.note: all means everyone

explanation.surface: A warning that nearly everyone overrun by vermin will turn hostile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' trims the last letter; 'beset by' then wraps the vermin round it. 'will show' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Malice is the wish to do harm, a form of hostility or ill will.

clue.text: Passage remains presented in speech, offering protection for viewer

indicators.note: speech means the words are spoken, so the answer is how they sound

parts.note: an aisle is a passage between rows of seats; ash is what remains after burning

explanation.surface: A speech about the remains in a passage somehow offers shelter to an onlooker.
explanation.walkthrough: AISLE + ASH said out loud sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyelashes shield the eye from dust, and the eye is what does the viewing.

clue.text: Many heading off in pursuit of refuge for poor people

indicators.note: pursuing means following behind, so this comes after the refuge

parts.note: a haven is a refuge

indicators.note: the heading is the first letter, which goes off

parts.note: lots means many

explanation.surface: Many set off after a place of safety for the needy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading off' removes the first letter of the word for many, and 'in pursuit of' puts what is left after the refuge.
explanation.definitionFit: The have-nots are the poor, contrasted with the haves who possess wealth.

clue.text: Artist showing limits to vanity and heartless cheek

indicators.note: read as 'limits to', the two end letters are put to either side of the word and, closing round it
the limits of vanity are its outermost letters, first and last
a heartless word loses its middle, keeping just its ends

explanation.surface: A painter is accused of vanity and cheek, with little heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'limits' takes the outer letters of vanity, and 'to' sets them either side of AND; 'heartless' empties cheek. The painter is often spelt Vandyke in English.
explanation.definitionFit: Anthony van Dyck was the Flemish painter famous for portraits at the court of Charles I.

clue.text: European city seen in October and November meeting

indicators.note: meeting means the two month names are joined end to end
the city is seen inside the two month names run together, so only the tail of the first month counts

parts.note: N is November in the radio alphabet, and also the first letter of the month

explanation.surface: A meeting in a European city scheduled across two autumn months.
explanation.walkthrough: Phi means the city to be seen across the join when the month names meet, with 'and' a link; this parse keeps the tail of October and adds N.
explanation.definitionFit: Bern is the Swiss federal capital, a city in Europe.

clue.text: English monarch dismissing first King's Mathematician

indicators.note: the opening letter of the monarch is dismissed

parts.note: a monarch is a ruler
R, from rex, stands for king

explanation.surface: An English monarch dismisses the first king's mathematician from court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dismissing first' removes R from RULER; the 's is 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Leonhard Euler was the prolific eighteenth-century Swiss mathematician.

clue.text: Russian director almost ready to probe 14?

indicators.note: probing means poking inside, so the short piece enters the scientist

parts.note: 14 refers to the answer at 14-down, a scientist, here Albert Einstein

indicators.note: almost means one letter short, so the last is cut

parts.note: set means ready

explanation.surface: A Russian film-maker nearly ready to investigate a scientist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims the word for ready, and 'to probe' sends the remainder into the scientist of 14-down.
explanation.definitionFit: Sergei Eisenstein was the Soviet film director of Battleship Potemkin.

clue.text: Drunk later today? That's not on

indicators.note: not means the little word is left out

parts.note: tonight is later today

explanation.surface: Someone plans to get drunk tonight, and another protests that it is unacceptable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That's not on' is an idiom for unacceptable; here 'not' takes ON out of TONIGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: Tight is informal for drunk, as in being tipsy.

clue.text: University recently adopting shortened term? Finally

indicators.note: to adopt is to take in, so the shortened word goes inside

parts.note: lately means recently

indicators.note: shortened means the last letter is cut

parts.note: a time is a term or period

explanation.surface: A university has lately taken on shorter terms at last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortened' trims the last letter, and 'adopting' has the word for recently take it in. 'Finally' at the end looks like an indicator but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Ultimately means in the end, finally.

clue.text: Early Hanoverian with hint of total determination

parts.note: GRI, Georgius Rex primus, is George I, first of the Hanoverian kings

indicators.note: a hint is just a trace, here the first letter

explanation.surface: An early Hanoverian king showing a trace of total resolve.
explanation.walkthrough: The Hanoverians were the German-born British royal house from 1714, starting with George I.
explanation.definitionFit: Grit is courage and resolve, so it means determination.

clue.text: British and French are adopting long trousers

indicators.note: to adopt is to take in, so the longing word goes inside these letters

parts.note: es is French for are, as in tu es
to itch is to long for something

explanation.surface: British and French people take to wearing long trousers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French are' gives ES, French for (you) are; BR and ES take in ITCH.
explanation.definitionFit: Britches is a variant of breeches, an informal word for trousers.

clue.text: By no means the leading set of equipment for a new pet

parts.note: a kit is a set of equipment
ten is far from number one, playfully imagining a series of kits numbered from one

explanation.surface: A shopper is told this isn't the best starter kit for a new pet.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke reads the answer as KIT TEN, far down a numbered list of kits.
explanation.definitionFit: A kitten is a young cat, often newly taken home as a pet.
